subject: Model fit & prompt set collection — Acme (P0)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@acme.io>, Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@acme.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit & prompt set collection — Acme (P0)

Hi Sana / Liam,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: Evaluate model fit for Acme's in-product assistant (FAQ + account lookup + light codegen).
- Success criteria: ~80% accuracy on intent classification, <1.2s p95 latency for short prompts, and no high-severity hallucinations on account lookup flows.

Action items we discussed:
1) Acme to share a representative prompt set (examples, edge cases, redaction notes) — Sana to send.
2) Redwood to run initial bench vs our curated models and share a short report + recommended configs.
3) If model/regression risks look acceptable, plan a small pilot (100k tokens/day) on Dedicated/Reserved capacity.

For prompt collection: we prefer a CSV with columns: prompt_id, user_prompt, expected_output (if available), category (faq/account_lookup/codegen), redaction_required (yes/no), notes. I attached a template below for your convenience. Also please include a short manifest of any sensitive fields we should redact or handle specially.

Preliminary model recommendations based on the call (we'll confirm after we get your prompts):
- Llama2-13B (quant q4) — good latency/cost balance for FAQ and general instructions.
- Mistral-Instruct (large) — strong for reasoning-heavy/code snippets.
- Redwood-curated 7B (opt) — useful as a lower-cost fallback for high-throughput routes.

I'll run a quick eval (classification + hallucination checks) once we have your CSV. Estimated turnaround: 3 business days for initial benchmarks.

Attached: prompt_collection_template.csv (template), and a short checklist for redaction.

Thanks — looking forward to the prompts.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@acme.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@acme.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit & prompt set collection — Acme (P0)

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the template. Attaching an initial dump of ~120 prompts we use in support flows; also attached a sensitive-fields manifest that lists internal IDs and PII fields.

High-level notes: many of the account_lookup prompts include internal account ids (e.g., acct_12345) and some include customer names and order numbers. We would like to keep all PII out of anything that leaves our systems. Happy to redact if you can confirm the suggested approach.

Files attached: acme_sample_prompts.csv, sensitive-fields-manifest.xlsx

A couple of edge cases to call out:
- Prompts that chain lookups ("Find user by email -> return last order details") — we care about hallucination risk here.
- Prompts with partial code snippets that expect the assistant to generate code to call internal APIs.
- Short, terse prompts with minimal context (mobile UX) — latency is important.

Let us know if you want more categories (we can add).

Best,
Sana
Head of Product, Integrations | Acme.io
sana.gupta@acme.io

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@acme.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit & prompt set collection — Acme (P0)

Thanks Sana — received the files, and appreciate the edge-case notes. We'll start the initial pass today. A few quick items / guidance on redaction and next steps: 

1) Redaction guidance
- For PII/IDs: please replace customer-facing names and any account IDs with stable placeholders (e.g., <PERSON_NAME>, <ACCOUNT_ID>). Keep a mapping internally if you need to rehydrate later.
- For order numbers or invoice ids: replace with <ORDER_ID>.
- For code snippets that reference internal endpoints: replace hostnames/keys with placeholders and include a short comment describing the expected external behavior.

2) Prompt collection best-practices
- Include an "expected_output" where possible for deterministic intents (FAQ/account_lookup). For codegen prompts include a short "acceptance_criteria" row.
- Mark prompts that must never leave the network (we can run evals inside your VPC/private deployment) — add column run_in_vpc=yes/no.

3) Recommended models & quick config notes (initial hypothesis):
- redwood/llama-2-13b-q4ok: baseline — balanced latency/cost. Use dynamic batching with max_seq=512 for FAQ routes.
- mistral-instruct-large: higher-quality for codegen/complex reasoning. Use temperature 0.0-0.2 for deterministic outputs.
- redwood/opt-7b-fp16: cost-sensitive routes as fallback.

4) Benchmarks & links
- We'll run: intent classification accuracy, hallucination check on lookup prompts (cross-check against expected_output where provided), and latency (p50/p95). Link to our initial benchmark template: https://drive.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-initial
- HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/67890

5) Timeline
- Initial pass + short report: ~3 business days after we get the cleaned CSV.
- If you'd like the eval to run inside your VPC for sensitive prompts, we can scope that as a separate task (estimate depends on infra access).

Attaching prompt_collection_template.csv (filled example) to show expected columns.

If Dev or Neha want to add technical runbook items, please chime in.

—
Marissa

From: Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@acme.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@acme.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 17:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit & prompt set collection — Acme (P0)

Thanks Marissa — that's exactly the guidance we needed. We'll: 
- Redact customer names/account IDs to <PERSON_NAME>/<ACCOUNT_ID> in the CSV.
- Mark sensitive prompts run_in_vpc=yes.
- Add expected_output for classification prompts and acceptance_criteria for codegen.

We'll send the cleaned CSV + a short mapping file by end of day tomorrow. Please confirm whether the initial eval will use the exact model names you listed (llama-2-13b-q4ok, mistral-instruct-large) or if Redwood will also include any smaller/faster variants in the same run.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sana
